q: Cash equity settlement in India follows:
e: T+1 settlement was fully implemented for all NSE/BSE listed cash equity in January 2023. T+0 is optional in two windows since 2024.

q: The two pay-in legs in cash equity settlement are:
e: Buyer pays funds; seller delivers securities (from demat). Both flow to clearing corp first, then CC pays out: funds to seller, securities to buyer.

o: Physical certificates can still be delivered
Securities are transferred electronically through NSDL/CDSL
e: Since 2019, India is fully demat. Physical certificates are not accepted in settlement. Securities transfer electronically through NSDL/CDSL.

q: If a seller fails to deliver securities on T+1, the clearing corp initiates:
e: Auction (buy-in) — CC buys equivalent securities from the market to deliver to the original buyer. Cost is charged to the defaulting seller.

q: Stock futures and stock options on expiry are settled by:
e: Stock F&O switched to mandatory physical delivery on expiry from October 2019. Index F&O continues to be cash-settled.

q: eDIS (electronic Demat Instruction Slip) authentication is via:
e: eDIS uses OTP authentication per transaction. Replacing PoA (broader authority) for client safety. SEBI is nudging brokers to migrate to eDIS.

q: T+0 settlement (since 2024) has cut-off windows of:
e: T+0: Window 1 closes 1:30 PM; Window 2 closes 3:30 PM. Voluntary opt-in for eligible stocks. Settled same evening.

q: On the ex-date for a corporate action in T+1 settlement, the price:
e: Ex-date = first day price trades without the entitlement (1 day before record date in T+1). Cum-prices traded before this; ex-prices trade from this day.

q: MTM settlement in F&O is paid:
o: Before market open the next day
e: MTM cash settlement happens before market open on T+1, debiting/crediting clearing members' accounts at designated clearing banks.

q: A bulk deal must be reported by:
e: Bulk deals (> 0.5% of company shares in a single day) must be reported same day to the exchange. Block deals (negotiated within ±1% of market) also reported promptly.

o: Stocks listed only on Indian exchanges
Indian shares listed on US/Global exchanges via depository
e: ADR (American Depository Receipt) — Indian co's shares listed on US exchanges via custody-and-depository structure. GDR — listed on multiple non-Indian exchanges.

o: Monetary settlement when auction fails or is impossible
e: Close-out = monetary compensation at exchange-determined price (typically high of trade day + buffer) when auction fails or isn't possible. No security delivered; defaulter pays.

q: An ITM (in-the-money) option on expiry is:
o: Held over to the next month
e: ITM options auto-exercised by clearing corp on expiry. Cash settled (index) or physically delivered (stock). OTM options expire worthless.

o: Each trading day's trades settle on a specific later day (T+1)
e: Rolling settlement = each day's trades settle on T+1 (current cycle). Replaced earlier 'fixed settlement' (weekly batches). India moved to T+1 in Jan 2023.

q: An OFS (Offer for Sale) is typically used by:
o: A promoter selling shares via the exchange to reduce stake
e: OFS = an exchange-based mechanism for promoters or large shareholders to sell shares (e.g. for SEBI's minimum public shareholding rules). Settled at auction-determined price.

q: When a record date for a dividend is announced as T+10, the ex-date is approximately:
o: T+9 (one trading day before record date)
e: In T+1 settlement, ex-date = one trading day before record date. So if record date is T+10, ex-date is approximately T+9. Holders on record date receive the dividend.

q: Settlement bank for a clearing member's pay-in:
e: Each CM has a designated 'clearing bank' approved by the CC. Pay-in funds debited from this account; pay-out credited there. SEBI maintains a list of approved clearing banks.

q: A block deal is defined as:
o: A trade > 1% of company shares in a single day
A negotiated trade within ±1% of market price
e: Block deal = pre-negotiated large trade within ±1% of market price, executed in a special window (9:00-9:15 AM and 2:05-2:20 PM). Reported same day. Bulk deal is the > 0.5% threshold.
